correctness.rationale: For each independent sampled index pair the normalized scalar hypergradient is exactly -alpha+h alpha^2/(2p_i) on a matching pair and zero otherwise. Its expected convex polynomial is -c alpha+h alpha^2/2. At alpha=c/h, coordinate i is multiplied by 1-c/p_i. The matched-pair events of probability p_i^2 recur almost surely and force contraction under all tie choices whenever c<2p_i. If c>=2p_i, pathwise absolute value cannot decrease from nonzero initial coordinate under any allowed tie choice. The exact raw mean-square factor and simplex maximum yield the d2 and d-dimensional exact phase boundaries. The independent standard-library Fraction checker passed 375 seeded model cases and 429 simplex-floor cases plus 4 exact finite-horizon state enumerations. No finite checks were used as substitutes for the proof. Each claim is limited to frozen population-target scalar steps.

The published closest scalar-curvature published-finding corpus full text has an always-positive validation curvature and a genuinely protective null step; its claims do not imply the independent disjoint-coordinate null-step failure. Arbitrary-sampling coordinate descent has a different step-design mechanism; available own results concern different dynamics. Residual priority risk is expressly recorded; a negative search alone is not presented as novelty proof.

value.rationale: Orthogonal data supports and unequal sampling occur naturally in sparse stochastic optimization. The exact c versus 2p_min threshold shows independent validation can be blind to a destructive proposal, even on an isotropic strongly convex objective with all sampled losses sharing its minimizer. The sharp universal minimum-sampling-mass frontier gives an actionable probability-design criterion, and the finite uniform four-component example demonstrates the issue without an exotic oracle. This is a structural phase classification, not simply numerical recomputation or a routine normalization check.
